claims.text: Tungsten and CuCrZr have a large mismatch in thermal expansion coefficients.
Tungsten and CuCrZr have substantially different melting points.
Direct bonding of tungsten to CuCrZr produces problematic residual stresses.
Directly bonded tungsten and CuCrZr are susceptible to detrimental inter-diffusion.
The proposed W-based RHEA interlayer would have a nanostructured, compositionally graded microstructure transitioning from tungsten-like to CuCrZr-compatible properties.
Composition tuning can give the proposed W-based RHEA an intermediate thermal expansion coefficient.
A graded W-based RHEA interlayer can mitigate the thermal expansion mismatch between tungsten and CuCrZr.
The proposed W-based RHEA can act as a robust diffusion barrier between tungsten and CuCrZr.
The graded interlayer would minimize interfacial stresses.
Nanocrystalline RHEAs can exhibit high thermal stability and resistance to irradiation damage.
The proposed interlayer would reduce microstructural degradation caused by ion irradiation and thermal cycling.
RHEAs possess strong elevated-temperature mechanical properties and are promising for advanced nuclear applications.
The graded RHEA interlayer would lower residual stresses relative to direct tungsten-to-CuCrZr bonding.
The graded RHEA interlayer would improve the mechanical integrity and reliability of the tungsten/CuCrZr joint.
The graded RHEA interlayer would reduce inter-diffusion between tungsten and CuCrZr under reactor conditions.
Successful long-term performance depends on retention of the interlayer's graded nanostructure and chemical stability during high-temperature exposure and irradiation.
